tagline: The safari republic's capital — fast-growing, friendly, and the gateway to Victoria Falls and South Luangwa's walking safaris.
overview: Lusaka is the capital of the country that invented the walking safari — a fast-growing, easygoing city of 3 million in a landlocked nation blessed with wildlife and the mightiest waterfall on earth.

The city itself is markets and momentum: the sprawling Soweto and Luburma markets, the Kabwata cultural village's craft stalls, and the restaurants and nightlife of the Kabulonga and Rhodes Park districts. It's friendly, functional, and improving fast.

Speed's 2025 Africa tour streamed from Lusaka. The bucket-list items are hours away: Victoria Falls at Livingstone ('the smoke that thunders') and South Luangwa National Park, where the walking safari was pioneered.

funFacts.text: 'Mosi-oa-Tunya' — the smoke that thunders — is Zambia's side of the world's largest waterfall.

funFacts.text: The maize-meal staple is the national plate — eaten with relish and hands.

funFacts.text: Lusaka was designed as a garden city in 1935 — it has sprawled wildly since.
